engagement_title: Lumen Quarterly Autumn issue: the boatyard feature spread, the cover off a scanned masthead, and the teasers that sell the single copy
vertical: Media, publishing and entertainment. An independent arts and culture quarterly published by a two person imprint in Portland, Maine, laying out its Autumn issue around one photo essay while holding a house style built by a designer who has left.
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com brand standards post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, where the client requires every piece to stay 'strictly inside my existing brand guidelines' and supplies 'the full style guide - logo lock-ups, colour palette, typography rules, imagery tone, even sample layouts', asking that 'each design feels cohesive with the rest of the brand'. Co-anchor: the Upwork print formatting post in the same ledger entry, a self publisher wanting files prepared to a stated trim with 'Bleed, margins, and resolution set to KDP specifications' and files that 'pass KDP's preflight check first time', which is where this engagement's print reality comes from. Both posts name no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional title Lumen Quarterly, published by the fictional Lumen House Press. No real publication, publisher, book, person or trademark is named, and the house typefaces are referred to by role rather than by name. The ledger's STRENGTHEN verdict keeps the concept (one issue, one look, cover plus spread plus teasers, everything editable through proofing) and deepens it, because CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) shows the honest fuller commission: the printer's own press file is a genuine structure inspection channel through convert_pdf_to_indd and export_idml, a masthead surviving only on a printed cover can be recovered as real vector, and mixed canvas sizes in one export make the cover, the spread and the teasers one editable document. It also shows what must be said out loud rather than promised, which is exactly what the print anchor is about.
client_one_liner: The Autumn feature is a fourteen frame photo essay shot across one moving afternoon, our masthead survives only on a printed cover we scanned, our style guide was written by a designer who left, and the editor will still be moving copy the week we ship.
client_brief:
Lumen Quarterly, Autumn issue

We are an independent arts and culture quarterly out of Portland, Maine. Two of us full time. Eighteen dollars an issue, sixty a year, and readers pay that because the thing is good to hold. Autumn goes to the printer in five weeks.

The issue turns on one feature: a photo essay from a boatbuilder's shop up the coast, fourteen frames, plus about two thousand words. We need the feature laid out as a spread somebody can actually read, the cover, the section opener that sits in front of it, and the teasers we post to sell single copies.

There is one more thing, because the issue is a thing people keep. Every Autumn we send our year subscribers a small set of plate cards, one card per photograph in the feature, the picture on the front and the caption and the photographer's credit underneath, and we sell the same set at the counter. Our card printer already runs a card for us and sent back the file he prints from. We need the set built off the same graded photographs as the issue, one card to a frame, so the cards and the magazine are unmistakably the same essay.

What we can give you. The essay as shot, across one afternoon, so the light moves through it. The editor's copy, which is final and cannot be cut. Our style guide, which our first designer made: lock ups, palette, type rules, imagery tone, sample layouts. We want the issue to sit strictly inside it, because the whole point of the title is that every issue feels like the same magazine. Our printer also sent back last Spring's file, the one they actually printed from, in case it helps you see how the page sits.

Our masthead is a problem. The artwork in the guide is a screenshot somebody pasted in. The only place it exists properly is the printed cover, which we scanned.

On the cover we want the masthead and one frame from the essay, and we like it when the type and the picture are properly interlocked rather than the type just sitting on top of everything.

All of it has to stay editable, because the editor moves copy right up to the file date and neither of us can rebuild a page.

And a note at the end: what you did, what we are actually set in, and anything about the print side you think we have wrong.
price_band_and_audience: Eighteen dollars a single issue and sixty dollars a year, readers 30 to 55, design literate, buying an object as much as an article. The band is load bearing. At this price the issue lives on typographic craft: a generous measure, real hierarchy, white space the eye rests in, pictures given room and sequence. Push it down into a busy tabloid grid (six stories a page, rules everywhere, tight leading, a cover shouting four cover lines) and the same content reads as a free listings paper, and nobody renews a sixty dollar subscription to a free listings paper. Push it up into an art book of eight words a page and no navigation and it stops being a magazine, loses the reader who wants the feature, and cannot carry the two thousand words the editor has already approved. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: An independent arts and culture quarterly, published four times a year around one long photo essay and its writing.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Published by Lumen House Press, a two person imprint in Portland, Maine, founded 2016.
brand_identity.about: Lumen Quarterly is a print magazine about art, craft and the people who make things along the coast. Each issue turns on one photo essay and about two thousand words of reporting. Readers pay for it because it is good to hold and worth keeping on a shelf, not for news.
brand_identity.audience: Design literate readers aged 30 to 55 who buy the object as much as the article and renew a subscription because the magazine is made with care.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Eighteen dollars a single copy, sixty dollars a year. An independent object priced above a newsstand title and below an art book, sold on typographic craft rather than volume.
brand_identity.typography: The whole product is the type. A refined display serif for the masthead and openers, a readable book face for the two thousand word body at a generous measure, a quiet sans for captions, credits and folios. Real hierarchy, white space the eye rests in.
brand_identity.voice: Considered, warm and exact, written like an essay rather than a pitch. Example line the brand would write: He has built the same hull the same way for forty years, and he still stops to look at the grain before the first cut.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The house style guide was made by the magazine's first designer, who has left, and it is now a couple of issues out of date on type. The masthead artwork inside the guide is a flattened screenshot, so the only proper record of the wordmark is the printed cover, which has been scanned. The printer also returned last season's press file.
brand_identity.values: Every issue should feel like the same magazine. Continuity of type, measure and picture treatment is the identity, and the reader should recognise Lumen before reading a word.

assets_supplied.name: lumen_autumn_essay/ (14 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: The feature photo essay from a boatbuilder's shop: workshop interiors, hands and tools, hull details, and two portraits, shot across one afternoon on two bodies.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The essay as shot. The light moves through it because it was all one afternoon."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One workshop frame's window is clipped to pure white, so a highlight recovery move returns a result in which nothing visibly changes, which reads as the tool failing rather than as the data being gone. Separately the lead portrait puts pale hair against a lime washed pale wall at almost the same luminance, so subject detection has no contrast along the hair and shoulder and hands back a bitten edge on that frame alone, at full success and clean at preview scale.

assets_supplied.name: lumen_spring_issue_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last Spring's feature opener and section opener exactly as the printer supplied them: a real press PDF with embedded font subsets.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What they printed from. It might help you see how the page sits."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the conversion exposes as editable frames is nothing like the printed page suggests: a spread that reads as a standfirst, two columns, three pull quotes and four captions can convert to a single continuous flow with no graphic frames at all. What that document does carry, the applied faces, sizes and measure, does not agree with what the supplied style guide states, and neither fact is visible without exporting and reading the document itself.

assets_supplied.name: lumen_style_guide.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The house style guide made by the magazine's first designer: lock ups, palette, type rules by role, imagery tone, and two sample layouts.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The guide. We want the issue to sit strictly inside it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is two issues out of date on type, naming a display weight the magazine stopped setting, and the masthead artwork inside it is a flattened screenshot pasted into the page rather than usable artwork. Its sample layouts also assume captions without credit lines, which the essay's captions all carry.

assets_supplied.name: lumen_cover_scan.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A flatbed scan of the printed Spring cover, the only place the masthead exists at size: a wide letterspaced wordmark in one ink over an uncoated stock.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The masthead, properly, from the printed cover."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Disjoint letterforms with tight counters on an absorbent uncoated stock, so the ink edge is soft and background removal keeps two or three letters and drops the rest while reporting success. Ink and stock also run close in value down the shadowed gutter third of the scan, and the trace comes back with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle at path zero.

assets_supplied.name: lumen_autumn_copy.md
assets_supplied.kind: The editor's final copy: the feature body of about two thousand words, the standfirst, three pull quotes, fourteen captions with credit lines, and five candidate cover lines.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The body runs roughly a fifth longer than last issue's feature, which the sample layouts were built around, and every caption carries a credit line the sample layout has no room for. Neither is stated anywhere in the copy or the guide.

assets_supplied.name: lumen_platecard_template.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The card printer's flat single-card press file for the Autumn plate-card set: one A6 landscape card carrying a plate image, a plate numeral, the frame's title, its caption and the photographer's credit, and the issue line, exactly as the printer runs it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer already runs for the plate set. This is the file he prints from."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the conversion exposes is nothing like the printed card: the plate numeral, the title, the caption and the credit line convert to a single continuous text story in one frame rather than four addressable fields, so the offset of each field is only knowable by reconstructing the story string, and the plate picture on the printer's sample was a page-level anchored image that flattens on conversion, so the converted document carries no graphic frame to bind a new picture into and the placeholder has to be built. The media box equals the trim, so there is no bleed box and a press-ready-with-bleed card cannot be honoured from it. None of this is visible without converting and reading the document itself.

assets_supplied.name: lumen_platecard_roster.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The plate roster the set is merged from: one row per essay frame carrying a plate number, the frame's title, its caption, the photographer's credit and the graded picture that belongs on that card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One card per picture in the feature, in the running order, off the same photographs as the issue."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The rows are in the editor's running order, which is not the frames' filename order, so the picture column is the only authority on which frame belongs on which plate and binding by row position mis-pairs them. The plate numbers are written three different ways across the rows and one number is repeated by a typing error, so naming one file per plate by its number collides and silently overwrites; two different plates also carry the same title. One row's credit cell is blank and has to be recovered from the copy, and the row for the clipped-window frame carries no picture at all because that frame cannot be brought to the issue look. None of this is revealed by any header.

acceptance_bar: The fourteen essay frames read as one afternoon in one workshop when they run in sequence: one white point, one warmth, one black point, one treatment. A frame that cannot be brought to the issue look is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.

The masthead is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and its counters still open at the size it actually reproduces on the cover, over the photograph.

On the cover the masthead and the picture are genuinely interlocked rather than the type sitting flat on top, and the cut edge that makes that possible holds along hair and shoulder at cover size, not only at preview scale.

The issue is ONE native editable Express document carrying the cover at true trim, the section opener, the feature spread pages and both teaser canvases, each root keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.

The feature body sets as real columns with a readable measure, not as a single reflowed block, and every pull quote and every caption including its credit line is present and set, on every page and not only the first.
Every photograph in the document is embedded image data rather than a reference, and no canvas shows an empty grey box where a picture should be.

All two thousand words of the editor's copy are present and set. Nothing is cut to make it fit, and if the copy does not fit the house measure the note says so and proposes the change rather than the layout losing a paragraph quietly.

One type system across the cover, the opener, the spread and the teasers, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight used, and stating plainly where the delivered issue follows the style guide and where it follows what the magazine actually prints.
The note states what was applied per photograph, every resize any tool reported, what the printer's file turned out to contain, and an honest account of what this route can and cannot hand a printer.

The Autumn plate-card set produces one card per essay frame that reached the issue look, page count equalling that plate count, each card carrying its own graded frame bound through the picture column and its own title, caption and photographer credit, with the row whose credit was blank recovered from the copy and the frame that could not be graded handled deliberately rather than shipped as a blank.

Every per-plate proof is identifiable and carries the record it claims, on a key that survives plate numbers written inconsistently and two plates sharing a title, and no plate silently binds a repeated or mis-paired picture.
Nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed that the supplied plate-card file cannot carry, and the shortfall is reported.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the issue. It fixes one issue look off the strongest frame and brings fourteen frames shot across a moving afternoon on two bodies toward it one call at a time, applies confined corrections where a whole frame move takes the varnished wood orange, lifts the three subjects the cover and the teasers need, cuts each picture to its picture box without ever enlarging, and recovers the masthead at ink level off a scan of an uncoated printed cover with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole issue as one native editable document: the cover at true millimetre trim, the section opener, the feature spread pages and both teaser canvases, each declaring its own canvas. This is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout, and it is what keeps the editor able to move copy up to the file date. Photographs must be inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the masthead goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, columns must be built as real containers, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The issue's type system, which is the whole product at this price. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so display, body, caption and folio are the agent's own art direction, judged against a design literate reader paying sixty dollars a year. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, an optical or display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by weight, every name has to be laundered into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign document inspection, print reference and data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (inventory mode and validator pass), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange and additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout (resolution, pageRange, createSeparateFiles)
adobe_surfaces.role: Two honest jobs on this one surface. First, the only way to learn what the magazine actually prints, as opposed to what its guide says: it converts the printer's own press file, exports the document structure to read the real frame inventory, applied faces, sizes and bounds, and renders the converted page at true print resolution as a scale reference for the measure and the margins. Second, the Autumn plate-card set, the one genuine one-record-per-page job here: the card printer's flat template is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the field offsets are computed from the document's own reconstructed story rather than from the mapping readout, a picture placeholder is built because the printed sample carries none, each row's own graded frame is bound through a prefixed picture column, and the run has to reach the counter as proofs whose plate identity is actually trustworthy. Everything the agent decides about the house grid, every place it chooses the shipped issue over the guide, and every plate that ships has to be defensible from what this surface returns.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one atmosphere frame the essay does not contain for the teaser set, IP clean, camera scale and with generative-tech candidates excluded on the flag rather than by eye, then graded into the issue look so it does not read as bought. The Boards half persists the picture edit the editor signs off from, which is a real editorial act on a fourteen frame essay, placed within the twelve per call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The cover, opener, spread and teasers are one authored fixed canvas document because the editor edits them until the file date. The printer's press file is an inspection input, not a template to merge. The brief pins both, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, plus the fact that the image tools enforce their own domain whitelist, so nothing reaches them except through this route or a licensed stock URL.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's Spring press file, export the document structure, and read what it actually contains: how many text frames, what bounds, what graphic frames, what faces and sizes are applied where.
trajectory.judgement: A printed page is no evidence of how a converted document is built, and frame granularity is not under the agent's control. Nothing about the house grid can be asserted until the document itself has been read.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory and applied type readout for last issue's opener and section opener.

trajectory.action: Render the converted page at true print resolution and reconcile what the shipped issue carries against what the style guide states, writing down every place the two disagree.
trajectory.judgement: The client asked for the issue to sit strictly inside the guide. Whether that instruction is even satisfiable is a finding, not an assumption, and where the two disagree the agent has to choose one and be able to defend it.
trajectory.produces: A scale reference of the printed page plus a written guide versus shipped issue reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen essay frames and the cover scan and triage them: which body, where in the afternoon, which are level, which carry clipped highlights, which subject runs close to its ground in value.
trajectory.judgement: One afternoon is not one light. The pictures are the only thing that can settle where the light moved and which frames will fight the sequence.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, clipping and subject contrast against the ground.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a boatyard interior full of horizontals shows a fraction of a degree.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one issue look off the strongest frame and bring each of the fourteen toward it with its own call, then apply confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a sequence, not fourteen good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong across a moving afternoon and two bodies, and warming the shop globally takes varnished wood orange while leaving the window cold.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut every frame to the picture box it fills on its destination page, reading the tradeoffs each call returns rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports an enlargement and it carries no warning language. Picture scale is also editorial: which frame runs full page and which runs small is the sequence argument.
trajectory.produces: Destination sized pictures with their returned tradeoffs recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for the one atmosphere frame the essay does not contain, filter to photography, read the generative-tech flag, license and download at full resolution, then bring it to the issue look.
trajectory.judgement: It has to survive sitting next to the essay. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the issue's world, with its cost recorded.

trajectory.action: Lift the subjects the cover and the teasers need: transparent for the cover interlock, and on the house ground for the teasers, reading every returned tradeoff and inspecting each edge at reproduction size rather than at preview scale.
trajectory.judgement: The interlock the client asked for only exists if the cut edge holds where the subject meets the ground. That is a property of each photograph and it is decided by looking, not by the response.
trajectory.produces: Subject plates, transparent and on ground, each with its returned tradeoffs and an edge inspection recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the masthead off the cover scan: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas path removed. Draw the folio rule and the section marks as inline SVG.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink and not the stock, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or the colour accurate plate is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on disjoint letterforms.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent masthead plus the issue's vector furniture.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, build one kit, and settle the guide versus shipped issue question in type.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a sixty dollar a year design literate reader. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and the choice between what the guide states and what the magazine actually prints has to be made once and applied everywhere.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role, and a stated position on the guide.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with every canvas as its own root at its own declared size, the feature body set as real column containers at the house measure, mixed weight and mixed colour runs inside the paragraphs, pull quotes and captions with credit lines, photographs inlined as image data, the masthead placed as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized left and top anchored wrapper, and family and weight declared on every text element. Then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is the measure, the sequence and how the cover holds four things at once.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole issue, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the cover, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at the cover is not looking at the spread.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected cover, and a per canvas markup audit for the opener, the spread and the teasers.

trajectory.action: Convert the card printer's plate-card template, export its structure and reconstruct its true story text, compute every field offset from that string rather than from the mapping readout, prepare the merge template with a built picture placeholder, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card reads as four tidy fields but the plate numeral, title, caption and credit convert to one continuous story, and the picture on the printer's sample was a flattened anchored image so there is no graphic frame to bind into until one is built. Validation returns valid on offsets computed from whatever string it is handed and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field or a picture placeholder landed is finding it in the re-exported document.
trajectory.produces: A plate-card merge template whose text placeholders and built picture placeholder are confirmed by inspection, plus the honest finding that no bleed can be introduced from this file.

trajectory.action: Loop back to imaging and cut the plate pictures from the graded masters to the card's picture proportion, reading the tradeoffs each crop returns, and reconcile them against the roster including the row that has no usable frame.
trajectory.judgement: The set has to be the same photographs as the issue, so the cards are cut from the graded masters and not re-graded, and cropping to the card proportion is a second destination crop off the same source that must not enlarge. The clipped-window frame that could not be brought to the issue look has no plate picture to cut, which is a decision to make before the run rather than a hole found on the printed sheet.
trajectory.produces: Card-proportion plate pictures at or below source scale with their returned tradeoffs recorded, and a stated treatment for the frame that has none.

trajectory.action: Run the plate roster against the template binding each row's own graded frame through the picture column, produce the printer's run and the per-plate proofs for the counter, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: Binding by row position mis-pairs the cards because the roster is in running order and not filename order, one picture repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, the plate numbering has to survive being written three different ways and repeated by a typo, two plates share a title so a by-title key collides, and a file's position in a returned list is not evidence of which plate is inside it because a multi-record raster run comes back in an order that does not match the roster.
trajectory.produces: The plate-card run with page count equal to the plates that reached the issue look, plus per-plate proofs each verified against its row.

trajectory.action: Create the picture edit board and add the graded essay and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, the vector masthead is not boardable, and the selection itself is the editorial work: which fourteen become the eight that run.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board carrying the picture edit with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the note: per photograph what was applied, every resize any tool reported, what the printer's file turned out to contain and where it disagrees with the guide, the type system by role, the copy fit position, how the plate-card run was delivered and each plate's identity confirmed, and an honest account of what this route can and cannot hand a printer.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes the guide is current and believes an editable file is a print file. Both need correcting plainly, with what to do instead, rather than being quietly worked around.
trajectory.produces: The written handover, including what could not be produced.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's file actually is once it has been converted and opened. The printed spread reads as a standfirst, two columns, three pull quotes and four captions, but the conversion's frame granularity is not under the agent's control and the whole page can arrive as one continuous flow with no graphic frames, in which case there is no per block grid to read off at all. Then the second finding: the faces, sizes and measure the document really carries do not match the style guide the client supplied and asked to be followed strictly, so the instruction the brief gives cannot be satisfied as stated. Neither fact appears anywhere except in the exported document.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because granularity is a property of the source file and the applied type is only readable after conversion and export. (b) Nothing states it: the client offers the printer's file as a courtesy and describes the guide as the thing to sit strictly inside. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different method for deriving the grid and a genuine editorial decision about which authority wins.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Derive the measure and the margins from the rendered page at true scale and from whatever frame bounds did survive, rather than from a per block inventory that does not exist, then reopen the type decision, choose between the guide and the shipped issue, and re-plan the spread around the authority chosen. Everything already sketched against the guide's sample layouts has to be re-judged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An Autumn issue set in a weight the magazine abandoned two issues ago and on a measure taken from a stale sample layout, delivered to a client whose single stated requirement was that every issue feel like the same magazine.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cover interlock the client asked for is possible from this photograph. Putting the masthead behind the subject means the subject has to be lifted cleanly, and on the lead portrait the pale hair meets a lime washed pale wall at almost the same luminance. Subject detection has no contrast to work with along the hair and the shoulder, so it returns a complete looking cutout at full success that is clean at preview scale and bitten along exactly the edge the cover puts against the masthead. Which frames behave this way is a property of each photograph and cannot be judged by looking at the uncut frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it; the alternative route, a material named selection of the wall inverted and filled, costs several calls and is what a competent agent adopts once the cheap route has been seen to bite. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the client likes the type and the picture interlocked. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the affected frame goes through a different chain, and the cover may end up carrying a different frame entirely.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the lift for that frame through an explicit selection of the ground by its own visual properties, inverted, rather than through subject detection, inspect the edge at cover size against the actual ground, and if it still will not hold, re-choose which essay frame carries the cover and re-cut the interlock around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A cover whose subject has a chewed hairline sitting directly against the masthead at full size, on the one page that has to sell the issue from a shelf, after every tool in the chain reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the constructions the spread is built on. The standfirst sits on a tinted band that lets the photograph read through it, which is authored the natural way as a blended layer, and the importer drops blend modes entirely so the band arrives as a plain opaque shape burying the picture underneath, with no warning and a successful response. In the same pass, whether the feature's columns survived as columns and whether the caption credit lines survived their runs can only be read from the returned per canvas markup, because the document's rendition returns the cover and nothing else. What survives, and whether what survives still reads as the page that was designed, exists only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a spread somebody can read and for the type and picture to interlock, which is art direction, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction upstream, a tint baked into the raster before it is inlined or a solid band re-judged for legibility, and then a re-composition of the page around it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the affected element as a raster prepared upstream or as a construction the importer keeps, re-judge legibility of the standfirst over the picture at real size, re-author the columns as containers that survive, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the cover.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A feature spread delivered as an editable file in which the standfirst sits on an opaque slab over the best picture in the essay and the body has reflowed into one long column, on the pages nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered plate proof actually contains the frame, caption and credit its filename claims. The natural way to hand the counter a proof per card is a multi-record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row labelled by row number. The labels do not hold: the files come back in an order that does not match the roster and nothing in the response says so, so a set named from the response has the wrong picture and the wrong caption under half the plate numbers. In the same run, the row whose credit cell was left blank binds an empty credit unless it was recovered from the copy first, and the plate for the frame that could not be graded either ships with no picture or is pulled, which changes the page count. What is actually inside each file exists only after the files are opened and read against their rows.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the mis-ordering is in the response itself and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would name the files from. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for one card per picture off the same photographs, and never characterises the delivery. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different delivery route entirely, either a single multi-page run whose page order is trustworthy, a createSeparateFiles run, or a per-record recordRange loop that produces one file at a time so identity is guaranteed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi-record raster route, re-run the plate set through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually inside it on a key that survives plate numbers written three ways and two plates sharing a title, recover the missing credit from the copy, and settle whether the clipped frame's plate ships or is pulled so the page count matches the plates that reached the issue look.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A subscriber set and a counter stack in which the caption and credit under a plate belong to a different photograph, printed and boxed, discovered by a reader who knows the essay rather than by the imprint.

deliverables.name: Autumn essay, graded to one issue look
deliverables.spec: Fourteen essay frames shot across a moving afternoon on two bodies brought to one issue target (one white point, one warmth, one black point, one treatment) plus the licensed atmosphere frame graded into the same world, each cut to the picture box it fills on its destination page, with no output exceeding its source pixel dimensions. Per frame parameter log including one line on why any frame differs from its neighbours, and the licensing record for the bought frame.

deliverables.name: Cover and teaser subject plates
deliverables.spec: Three subjects lifted from the essay: one for the cover interlock as a genuine transparent plate whose edge holds along hair and shoulder at cover reproduction size, and two for the teaser canvases composited onto the house ground in one call so the ground is part of the raster. One cut logic across the set, every returned tradeoff recorded, and no plate reaching its size by interpolation.

deliverables.name: Recovered Lumen masthead and issue furniture
deliverables.spec: The letterspaced masthead recovered from a scan of the printed cover as placeable, scalable vector geometry on a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, delivered as a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, with its counters still open at the size it reproduces on the cover over a photograph and reversed on the ground the teasers use. Paired with the folio rule and the section marks drawn as inline SVG so they arrive as editable vector rather than as pictures.

deliverables.name: Autumn issue document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying the cover at true millimetre trim, the section opener, the feature spread pages and both teaser canvases, each root keeping its own canvas size. Live editable text in one licensed type system, all two thousand words of the editor's copy set as real columns at the house measure, pull quotes and captions with their credit lines, the masthead as real vector shapes, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half: the editor moves copy up to the file date and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Autumn plate-card set
deliverables.spec: The card printer's flat press file reverse engineered into a live merge template with every text placeholder and the built picture placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the plate roster: one card per essay frame that reached the issue look, page count equal to that plate count, each card binding its own graded frame through the picture column and its own title, caption and photographer credit, with the row whose credit was blank recovered from the copy and the frame that could not be graded handled deliberately rather than left as a hole. Delivered as the printer's run plus per-plate proofs named from what is actually inside them on a key that survives plate numbers written inconsistently and two plates sharing a title, with the no-bleed reality of the supplied card file stated.

deliverables.name: Grid and type basis, handover note and picture edit board
deliverables.spec: An authored basis canvas recording the grid, the measure, the type roles and the picture treatment as the issue actually uses them, plus a written note recording per photograph what was applied, every resize any tool reported, what the printer's file turned out to contain and every place it disagrees with the supplied style guide, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, the copy fit position, and an honest statement of what this route can and cannot hand a printer. Paired with a persistent shareable picture edit board carrying the graded essay with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered image exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from, and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel dimensions of every delivered file against the manifest, and diff every captured tradeoffs object against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The cover plate carries genuine alpha rather than a white rectangle, and the teaser plates sit on the declared house ground.
verifiers_auto.how: Inspect the alpha channel of the cover plate for partial alpha at the subject boundary and full transparency at the frame corners, and read the corner pixels of the teaser plates.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered masthead's SVG has a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned every expected canvas, each keeping its own declared canvas size, with the cover at the stated 210 x 273 mm trim.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per slide width and height in the export response; assert every authored canvas is present each at its own declared size, and assert the cover canvas equals the 210 x 273 mm magazine trim converted at 96 dpi (210 mm = 793.7 px, 273 mm = 1031.8 px, i.e. 794 x 1032 px within +/- 1 px rounding).

verifiers_auto.text: No canvas resolved an image to the importer's placeholder, and the masthead arrived as vector path shapes rather than as one picture.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per canvas markup for 1x1 placeholder image data and count path shape elements in the masthead region on the cover.

verifiers_auto.text: The feature body arrived as multiple column containers rather than one reflowed block, and every pull quote and every caption credit line is present in the markup.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per canvas markup for the spread roots: assert 2 or more column containers are present (not one reflowed single block), and match all 3 pull-quote strings (PQ1, PQ2, PQ3) and all 14 caption credit lines (C01 through C14, each ending 'Photograph: Perrin Doyle') against the editor's copy file.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font-family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_auto.text: The full word count of the editor's copy is present in the document, with nothing cut.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract every text node from the returned markup and diff the concatenated body against the supplied copy file.

verifiers_auto.text: The plate-card merge template's re-exported interchange file contains every expected text placeholder and a bindable picture placeholder, and the printer's run page count equals the count of plates that reached the issue look.
verifiers_auto.how: Unzip the interchange file and grep the story files for all five text field placeholders (plate number, title, caption, credit, issue line) and the one built picture placeholder, then read the merged output's page count and assert it equals 13 (the 14 roster rows minus the single clipped-window plate for essay frame 02, whose Picture cell is blank and which is pulled because that frame cannot be brought to the issue look).

verifiers_auto.text: Every per-plate proof binds its own frame and carries its own title, caption and credit, no picture is repeated across plates, and no two proof files share a name.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the rendered text and placed image of each proof, match the caption and credit against the roster row and the copy file, diff the placed images for duplication, and list the filenames for collisions.

verifiers_auto.text: The picture-edit board was created and carries the intended edit with nothing silently dropped: the board exists and every item submitted for placement landed with no failed entries.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the boards_create_new_board response for a returned board id, then read the boards_add_items_to_board response(s) and assert the total placed item count equals the number of graded essay frames plus the licensed atmosphere frame that were submitted (the vector masthead excluded as non-boardable), across however many calls the 12-placements-per-call cap requires, with an empty failedItems array on every call (a 201 partial success carrying any failed entry fails this check).

verifiers_auto.text: The standfirst tint band did not arrive as an opaque slab burying the hero photograph, even though the importer drops blend modes: the photograph still reads behind the standfirst.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per canvas markup for the feature opener/spread standfirst region and assert the hero photograph's embedded image data is present behind the standfirst and is not fully occluded: any tint band shape over it must carry fill-opacity/alpha below 1.0, or the tint must be baked into the inlined photograph raster with no separate covering shape. A full-opacity solid fill rectangle that spans and covers the photograph fails this check.

verifiers_human.text: Run in sequence, the fourteen frames read as one afternoon in one workshop rather than as two cameras across a shifting light.
verifiers_human.how: Place the graded essay in the running order at page scale and judge white point, warmth, black point and treatment as a sequence.

verifiers_human.text: The cover interlock holds: the masthead sits behind the subject convincingly and the cut edge is clean along hair and shoulder at cover size.
verifiers_human.how: View the exported cover at reproduction size, not at preview scale, and look specifically where the subject meets the masthead.

verifiers_human.text: The masthead's counters are open at cover size and it still reads as the same masthead reversed on the teaser ground.
verifiers_human.how: View the mark at its reproduction size on the cover and on the teasers, not at full canvas.

verifiers_human.text: The feature spread is readable: the measure holds, the columns are columns, the pull quotes sit in the flow and every caption carries its credit.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported document and read the spread pages in Express as a reader would.

verifiers_human.text: The issue reads as an eighteen dollar object worth a sixty dollar subscription, not as a free listings paper and not as an art book that lost the article.
verifiers_human.how: Judge measure, hierarchy, white space, picture scale and cover restraint against the stated band and reader.

verifiers_human.text: The cover, the opener, the spread and the teasers read as one issue of one magazine rather than four designs sharing a masthead.
verifiers_human.how: View every canvas in sequence and judge grid, type, picture treatment and colour as one system.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the publishers something they did not already know, including the guide's staleness, the copy fit position and what could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that the guide versus shipped issue reconciliation, every resize and every limitation are named with what to do instead.

verifiers_human.text: Every plate card carries the right photograph with its own caption and credit, and the set reads as the same essay as the issue rather than a different selection.
verifiers_human.how: Open the per-plate proofs against the running order, starting with the plate whose credit cell was blank and the frame that could not be graded, and judge the graded look of the cards against the issue.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and what the printer's press file is actually for, given it is an inspection input rather than a template.
Whether the house grid can be read per block at all from the converted file, and what to derive the measure and margins from when it cannot.
Guide or shipped issue, once the two are known to disagree, and how to state that choice to a client whose only requirement was that every issue feel the same.
How far to push a moving afternoon toward one look before a frame stops being worth saving, versus naming it, including the frame whose window has no data left to recover.
Which route to lift the cover subject by, given that subject detection has nothing to work with where hair and wall share luminance and the alternative costs several calls.
Which essay frame carries the cover at all, judged on whether its edge can hold against the masthead rather than on whether it is the best photograph.

Selection prompt wording on the cover scan: naming the cover takes the stock, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the masthead, and background removal on disjoint letterforms is the wrong instrument entirely.
The type pairing across display, body, caption and folio, which the recommender refuses to make, plus the real numeric weight per family and the slug a display cut is actually reached by.
How to hold two thousand words that run a fifth long, plus captions carrying credits the sample layout has no room for, when the copy is declared final and cannot be cut.
What to tell a publisher who believes an editable file is a print file, including what this route cannot introduce and what the printer will therefore need from them.

Which plate-card delivery route carries per-plate identity safely, given a multi-record raster run comes back in an order that does not match the roster, and what key names a proof when the plate numbers are written three different ways and repeated by a typo and two plates share a title.

Whether to bind each plate by the picture column or the row position given the roster runs in the editor's order and not the frames' filename order, and whether the clipped-window frame's plate ships, is pulled, or runs without a picture.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome magazine that is not this magazine. IDENTITY: the feature is these fourteen photographs of this boatbuilder, the words are the editor's final copy which cannot be cut or paraphrased, and the masthead must be RECOVERED off a scan of the printed cover rather than redrawn, because a regenerated masthead is a different title. SPEC: the cover is a true trim canvas, the body is two thousand approved words that must all be present and set, every caption carries a credit line, and the house measure has to be derived from what the magazine actually prints. EDITABILITY: the issue is defined by staying editable, since the editor moves copy up to the file date and a two person imprint cannot rebuild a page. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: what the printer's file actually contains, whether this cutout holds where hair meets a pale wall, whether the standfirst band survived the import on a page the preview will not show. MERGE: the plate-card set is a one-record-per-page variable-data run, one card per photograph, page count equal to the plates that reached the issue look, each card bound to its own graded frame and its own caption and credit through a picture column that a generated sheet of handsome cards neither satisfies nor can be checked for, and whose per-plate identity is only trustworthy after the files are opened and read against the roster.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale_factor, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, and alpha survives crops at outputFileType png (13,371 partial alpha pixels preserved), so the cover plate is real. The cutout checkpoint rests on documented findings: remove_background kept only two letter fragments of a disjoint wordmark (1,743 opaque pixels of roughly 18,000 of ink), and the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry is a live observation, as are the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero on every trace. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd on a real font embedding PDF, export_idml as a genuine structure inspection channel returning frame counts, bounds, applied fonts and sizes, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as the frame inventory readout and validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, and document_render_layout at resolution 300 with createSeparateFiles returning true 2550x3300 raster are all verified end to end, fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page for a PDF derived template and page count equal to row count. The conversion checkpoint rests on the observed collapse of a six line flow to ONE TextFrame with zero graphic frames, and the plate-card proof checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi-record PNG and JPEG output comes back REVERSED while the response labels it by row, with a single multi-page PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes. The plate picture is bound through a prefixed picture column and additionalImageFiles, the picture placeholder is built because the PDF derived template exposes no graphic frame, and no bleed claim is made anywhere, because bleed cannot be introduced through a PDF derived template and pdfPreset is unusable. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, mm canvases resolve exactly at 96 dpi, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, mixed weight and mixed colour inline runs survive as spans inside one text frame, flex containers survive, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. The import checkpoint rests on the documented drops of mix-blend-mode and of column-count, both at HTTP success. Photos are base64 inlined because every external URL resolved to a placeholder, and transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, including the non-standard numeric weights and the separate slug for display cuts. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, isGenTech exposed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no generative expand, no fill_text, no animate_design, no font identification from an image, no batch above 20.
